clue.text: Snap after everyone starts imposing

indicators.note: after puts the photo word behind the opening letter
starts asks for the opening letter of the word everyone

parts.note: a snap is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: A photograph taken just as a crowd begins to throw its weight around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epic is grand and on a heroic scale, so it is imposing.

clue.text: Cast out to rehearse for inattentive audience?

indicators.note: a careless listener would mishear one word as a near-identical one, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: to rehearse is to practise, to exercise a skill

explanation.surface: An actor asked to run through lines for a crowd that is not paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the sound-alike is approximate: the two words differ only in one unstressed vowel, which an inattentive listener would miss.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise a demon is to drive it out, to cast it out.

clue.text: Absolutely determined to trade in old car

indicators.note: trading swaps things around, so the letters of these words are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone firmly resolved to part-exchange an old car at the dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade in' reads as one phrase in the surface, but 'in' is part of the fodder: IN + OLD + CAR rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironclad resolve or guarantee is one that cannot be broken, rigidly fixed.

clue.text: Public vote, for a change, best clip one at end of Grease

indicators.note: changing the letters around signals an anagram of the words before

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: at end of asks for the final letter of the film title Grease

explanation.surface: A public vote on swapping in a different best clip at the end of the musical film Grease.
explanation.definitionFit: A plebiscite is a referendum in which the whole electorate votes on one question.

clue.text: In which one's up in the air or close to the ground

definitions.text: In which one's up in the air or close to the ground

parts.words: In which one's up in the air or close to the ground
parts.note: one sense is a state of uncertainty, being undecided or up in the air; the other is the Caribbean dance in which one bends back to pass under a low bar near the floor

explanation.surface: A riddle about a place where one is either aloft or nearly on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a state of suspended uncertainty and a dance under a lowered bar, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Supporter's one going down the pub

indicators.note: in a down clue, going down means a letter moves lower, later in the word

parts.note: a supporter is a bra, in full a brassiere; the 's is no letter
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A football fan who heads off to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going down' moves the I of BRASSIERE two places further down the word, giving BRASSERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal restaurant serving drinks, loosely a bar or pub.

clue.text: Do a sonnet differently, below stage, for TV show

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the rearranged letters under the first piece

parts.note: a stage in a process is a step

indicators.note: arranged differently signals an anagram of the words before it

explanation.surface: Writing a sonnet in an unusual way, under the stage, for a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges DO A SONNET into TOEANDSON. STEPTOE AND SON was a BBC sitcom (1962-74) about a father and son who were rag-and-bone men.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a classic British television situation comedy.

clue.text: Confirmation of taxmen's presence, perhaps, that inflames viewer

parts.note: IR, the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority, stands for the taxmen being there
'it is' is a reply confirming something

explanation.surface: Proof that the tax inspectors are present, which enrages whoever is watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'IR? It is', confirming the taxmen are there; 'perhaps' flags the playful reading. The 'viewer' is the eye, and this condition inflames part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iritis is inflammation of the iris, part of the eye, which is the viewer.

clue.text: Go keenly at regular intervals around work unit

indicators.note: around puts the picked letters on both sides of the unit
taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of keenly, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Set off eagerly, pausing now and then around the factory section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like the start of the surface verb phrase but is the definition, the noun meaning vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means vigour, drive or pep, which is energy.

clue.text: American native with nothing on, I hesitate to say

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a plan that is on is possible, shortened to poss
um is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: A Native American wearing nothing at all, though the speaker is shy to say so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link ('with nothing on') but gives POSS, the short form of possible, as in 'is that on?'; 'with' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsupial is native to the Americas, the only one found there.

clue.text: Modern piano and organ found in chest outside gallery

indicators.note: outside puts the two joined pieces around the gallery

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for playing softly, so soft
the Tate is a London art gallery
the organ that sits in the chest is the heart

explanation.surface: Up-to-date instruments, a piano and organ, stored in a chest outside an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano and organ' look like instruments: piano is the softness marking and the organ is the one in the body. SOFTHEART goes outside TATE, which lands after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: State of the art describes the most advanced, up-to-date technology, so modern.

clue.text: Half a whale, the other half a fish

indicators.note: half asks for the back part of the word whale, its final three letters

parts.note: one's other half is a spouse, a wife

explanation.surface: A grotesque creature: half whale, half fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other half' looks like the second half of the creature, but it is the colloquial name for a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Prepares to fire rounds at ducks and other birds

indicators.note: rounds is read as a verb, the gun-readying word circling the others

parts.note: to cock a gun is to prepare it to fire
a duck is a score of nothing, O, so ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: A hunter readies his gun and fires shots at ducks and other birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like ammunition fired at the ducks, but it is the verb of surrounding, and 'ducks' are cricket scores of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockatoos are crested parrots, birds other than the ducks just mentioned.

clue.text: Object to having ice-cream, not guacamole, for starters

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to ice-cream rather than guacamole as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object to' reads as a verb phrase, but 'Object' alone is the noun definition and 'to' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object or item.

clue.text: Catch the overnight sleeper: one may roll by

parts.note: a skate is a flatfish, an angler's catch
a boarder lodges and sleeps at a house or school

explanation.surface: Advice to board the night train with sleeping berths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeper' suggests a railway sleeper train, but it is a lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on a wheeled board rolls past, so is one who may roll by.

clue.text: Arm pious women's organisation for campaigns

indicators.note: organising the letters puts them into a new order

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for women; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Equip a devout women's group for its campaigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like the women's group, but it signals rearranging ARMPIOUSW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Opium Wars were nineteenth-century conflicts between Britain and China, military campaigns.

clue.text: Site of temple ruins initially moving old woman to climb up

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing up reverses the whole run of letters
initially asks for the first letter of ruins

parts.note: astir means up and moving about
one's old woman is one's mother, Ma

explanation.surface: Ruins of a temple, where an elderly woman is set climbing upward.
explanation.walkthrough: R + ASTIR + MA gives RASTIRMA, which 'to climb up' turns upwards to read AMRITSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar in the Punjab is home to the Golden Temple, the holiest Sikh shrine.

clue.text: Means to follow sub coming on

indicators.note: to follow puts the method word after the other piece

parts.note: sub is a prefix meaning under
a means is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A method for trailing a submarine as it comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub' suggests a submarine or substitute, but here it is the Latin prefix for under.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under way is in progress, coming along.

clue.text: Commend a fine, stirring, novella

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters of the words before into a new order

explanation.surface: Praising a fine and exciting short novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' reads as praise for the book but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is John Steinbeck's 1937 novella about migrant ranch workers.

clue.text: Old admiral getting Scottish crown to surrender

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain peak, a summit or crown of the land
to bow is to yield or give way

explanation.surface: A naval officer of old forced to give up the crown of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: John Benbow was a celebrated English admiral of the late seventeenth century.

clue.text: Boot PC, perhaps, to get going

parts.note: to boot is to kick
politically correct is an example of what is acceptable or fashionable, in

explanation.surface: Restart a personal computer to get it running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot PC' looks like starting a computer; 'boot' is kick and 'PC' stands for politically correct, a sense of 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: When something kicks in it starts to take effect.

clue.text: Girl's correct writing letter that Eliza neglected

parts.note: to edit is to correct written work
Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady drops her aitches

explanation.surface: A young woman correcting her writing, dropping a letter the way Eliza did.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle, the cockney flower girl of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, famously drops her Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a female first name, and a girl is defined by example of one such name.

clue.text: Night light for bunk

definitions.meaning: the light given off by the moon at night

explanation.surface: A small lamp for the bed in a dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine means both the light of the moon and foolish nonsense.

clue.text: Lifting herb, mother's stuffing game with hands

indicators.note: Lifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
stuffing means the letters sit inside the words herb and mother's

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Raising a herb and mother's stuffing for a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'stuffing' into the definition, but it is the signal that the letters are tucked inside 'herb, mother's'; the definition is 'game with hands'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old card game, played in hands of cards.

clue.text: Ladies' answer to cook that's short and sweet

indicators.note: short means the cooking word loses its last letter

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
the ladies' is a women's lavatory, a lav

explanation.surface: A women's group answers how to make something brief and sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short and sweet' is a stock phrase, but 'short' trims BAKE to BAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Baklava is a sweet pastry of filo, nuts and honey.

clue.text: Gang had butcher's cutter

parts.note: a gang is a band of people
butcher's is rhyming slang, butcher's hook for look; had a look means saw

explanation.surface: A criminal gang owned a butcher's cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher's' suggests a meat shop, but in cockney rhyming slang a butcher's (hook) is a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsaw is a power saw with a looped blade, a cutting machine.

clue.text: With one clear bloomer, judge turning to drink

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to clear a profit is to net it
an aster is a flowering plant, a bloomer

explanation.surface: A judge who takes to the bottle after one obvious blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flower; the definition is someone who judges what they turn to, the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine taster is a judge of drink, assessing wines by sampling them.

clue.text: Pretentious Head off to celebrate

indicators.note: with its head off, the celebrating word loses its first letter

parts.note: to party is to celebrate

explanation.surface: A self-important headteacher leaves to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes something showily or affectedly artistic.
